div.l: This pardoner had heer as yolowe as wax
But smothe yt henge as doth a strike of flax
By ownces heng his lokkes that he hadde
And ther wyth he his sholdres oủerspradde.
But thynne it lay by culpons on and oon
But hood for Iolyte wered he noon
For hit was trussed vp in his walet
Him thought he rood al of the new get
Discheuele saue his cappe he rood al bare
Swich glaryng eyen had he as an hare
A vernycle had he sewed on his cappe
His walet by forn him in his lappe.
Bretful of pardoıı̄un comen fro Rome al. hoot
A voice he hadde as smal as hath a goot
No berd had he ne neủer sholde have
As smothe it was as it were late y shaue.
I trowe he were a geldyng or a mare
But of his qafte from berwyk vn to ware.
Ne was ther swych a nother pardoner
For in his male he hadde a pylow bere
Which that he seide was oure lady vaile
He seyde he had a gobet of the saile
That seint petre had whan that he went
Vppon the see til. IħuIhesu criste him hent
He had a croys of laton ful of stones
And in a glas he had pygges bones
But wyth thise relikes whan that he foond
A poủere ꝑperson dwellyng vppon lond
Vppon a day he gate him more moneye
Than that the ꝑpersoun gat in monthes twaye.
And thus wyth feyned flatery and Iapes
He maad the ꝑpersoun and the people his apes
But trewly to tellen at the last
He was in chirche a noble ecclesiast
Wel coude he reed a lesson or a story·
But altherbest he sang an offratory·
For wel he wist whan that song was songe
He moste p̉reche and wel afile his tonge
To wynne siluer as he ful wel coude
